prompt: We are a Series A company with 15 engineers. The team is pushing hard to rewrite our monolithic Node.js backend into Go microservices because deploys are getting slow.
expected: Applies Series A stage, advises against big-bang rewrite, points at deploy bottleneck and strangler/extract, classifies door, and states cost in weeks vs quarters.
actual: Series A / ~15 engineers: foundations and tech leads, not a full rewrite. Treat big-bang Go microservices as irreversible and high-cost (often 2–3× estimate while freezing features). First measure the deploy bottleneck (CI, tests, artifact size). Keep the monolith until team-level deploy contention is weekly; if one component truly blocks, extract only that slice via strangler fig (references/debt.md + architecture.md). Default: fix the pipeline (reversible, weeks) over rewrite (quarters of lost product velocity).

prompt: Should we build our own authentication service or use Auth0? We're a Seed stage startup with 4 engineers.
expected: Seed defaults to buy for commodity auth, frames TCO with upkeep, requires exit/export path, and classifies the door.
actual: Seed / 4 engineers: default buy (Auth0 or similar) unless you are an identity company. Auth is not core IP at this stage; build TCO is estimate×~2 plus ongoing upkeep (one engineer-month/quarter often exceeds typical SaaS before opportunity cost). Negotiate data export before signing so the door stays two-way. Escape hatch: revisit build only when scale, compliance, or differentiation makes buy untenable.

prompt: Our board wants 99.99% uptime and daily deploys. We have 8 engineers and page 5 times a night.
expected: Uses DORA/error-budget framing, challenges extra nines cost, prioritizes alert noise and on-call sustainability before vanity SLOs, and routes to operations reference.
actual: With 8 engineers and ~5 pages/night, on-call is already past a sustainable load—fix alert noise and runbooks before promising 99.99%. Each extra nine roughly multiplies reliability cost; many products cannot distinguish 99.9 from 99.99 given client-side variance. Set an SLO and error budget both sides accept (SRE framing), improve lead time and change failure with smaller releases/flags, then raise deploy frequency. Load references/operations.md for DORA bands, error budgets, and rotation sizing; translate to the board as risk + investment, not architecture slogans.
